newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians to restrict imports from Israel.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians to restrict imports from Israel.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority said on Tuesday Israeli companies wishing to export to the West Bank and Gaza Strip would need a Palestinian agent in the area starting January 1.

But Palestinian Minister of Trade and Industry Maher al-Masri reassured a delegation of Israeli businessmen during a meeting in the West Bank, saying the regulations would be implemented gradually to prevent any shock to the business communities on both sides.
"These regulations and this law has been implemented gradually in the past and we intend to carry on with the implementation of these regulations," Masri said.

"However, this does not mean that we are going to make any shocks within the business community on both sides. This does not mean the obstruction of the flow of commodities between both sides," he said.
Masri said negotiations were underway between Palestinian businessmen and Israeli and international companies to register franchises and agencies in the Palestinian self-rule areas.
He said some Israeli and foreign companies have also registered in the Palestinian Ministry of Trade and Industry.
The Palestinian Authority, which took over parts of the West Bank and Gaza under a 1993 self-rule deal, has eased dependence on the Israeli economy, bolstering trade with Jordan and Egypt.

Israel made the West Bank and Gaza Strip an exclusive market for its products during nearly three decades of occupation. Palestinian trade officials say prior to the self-rule deal, up to 95 percent of Palestinian imports came from or through Israel.
Danny Gillerman, head of the Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce, said after the meeting that the regulations would initially affect only some products.

"(They) will, for a start, be specific to certain goods but not all-encompassing...They will not be in any way a barrier or a boycott to Israeli goods or to imported goods from Israel entering the Palestinian Authority," he said.

Palestinian trade officials announced plans in August to stop Israeli franchises from selling products in the West Bank and Gaza in order to encourage Palestinian companies to replace them. Israel has said these regulations violate a 1994 economic accord which established a free trade area between the sides.

The regulations would affect various industries, including soft drinks and foodstuffs. The Palestinian Authority has already banned Israeli importers from selling certain brands of cigarettes and vehicles in the self-rule areas, allowing only Palestinian-imported goods.
Masri said the Palestinian Authority would make a list of the goods which would initially be affected by the regulations.
Gillerman said some Israeli industries will suffer from the new Palestinian regulations. But he said that the possibility of joint Israeli-Palestinian ventures may help alleviate the problem.
